articles.title: Ancient Egyptian princesses were buried with weapons. Their bones reveal why
articles.summary: Weapons buried with ancient Egyptian princesses may have been more than ceremonial decorations. Researchers studying royal mummies from Dahshur found bone changes consistent with years of archery and other strenuous weapon use. Several women also showed evidence of healed injuries, suggesting surprisingly active lifestyles that may have included hunting or military training.
articles.content:
For years, archaeologists have debated why some ancient Egyptian princesses were buried with weapons. The bows, arrows, daggers, and maces found in their tombs were often interpreted as ceremonial objects rather than equipment the women had actually used. A new examination of royal mummies from Egypt's Middle Kingdom now suggests that at least some of these women were physically trained to handle such weapons.

"Members of the royal family, especially the women, were active participants in skilled, physically demanding activities such as archery and hunting," said Dr. Zeinab Hashesh, lead author of the article in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology. "This conclusion is supported by the way their bones developed to sustain heavy muscle use, which corresponds directly to the weapons discovered in their tombs."

Royal Mummies Rediscovered at Dahshur

The research focused on six royal mummies originally uncovered during the 1890s at Dahshur, an Egyptian burial complex containing pyramids and shaft tombs. The remains later disappeared from scholarly attention for many years before being identified again in the Egyptian Museum during a curation project in 2020.

Four of the six individuals were sisters and daughters of the pharaoh Amenemhat II. They had been placed in matching underground burial chambers. Princess Ita was buried beside Princess Khenmet, while Princess Itaweret was interred alongside an unidentified woman who has tentatively been identified as Princess Sathathormeryt.

Their tombs contained objects more commonly associated with male burials, including bows and arrows. Princess Ita's coffin also held an especially ornate dagger. Similar royal objects were found with the two other individuals included in the investigation, Princess Noub-Hotep and King Hor.

All six bodies had been carefully mummified, but preservation was incomplete. Their soft tissues had deteriorated into powder, while portions of the skeletons were also missing. The princesses' skulls, for example, were lost during the early 1900s.

Even so, enough skeletal material survived in good condition for researchers to estimate age at death, height, and sex. The bones also provided evidence of past injuries, illnesses, and other aspects of the individuals' health.

Bones Reveal Archery and Weapon Use

"Princess Ita was a young woman aged between 28 and 34 with strong upper-body muscle attachments, suggesting she habitually used weapons like maces or daggers," said Hashesh. "Princess Khenmet was a woman in her late 30s or 40s who showed signs of thinning bones, but had very robust ligament attachments. Princess Itaweret was a young woman aged between 20 and 34 who survived broken ribs and foot fractures; her skeleton shows she was a skilled archer."

The sisters' skeletons contained unusually robust muscle attachments, indicating that they regularly performed strenuous physical activities. Those patterns closely match the movements required to use the weapons placed in their graves. Comparable skeletal evidence also suggests that Princess Noub-Hotep and King Hor practiced archery.

"We found pronounced development in the upper limbs of these individuals, which correlates to repetitive, high-intensity actions like pulling a bowstring or stabilizing a weapon, proving these activities were habitual throughout their lives," explained Hashesh. "This directly explains the presence of bows, arrows, and maces in the women's tombs; these were not just symbolic gifts but tools they actively used."

The findings suggest that repeated weapon use was part of these royals' lives rather than an occasional activity. Their physical development points to long-term practice involving demanding movements such as drawing a bowstring or controlling a weapon.

Injuries Point to Physically Demanding Lives

Several of the individuals also showed evidence of trauma, infections, and nutritional deficiencies. Princess Itaweret had suffered broken ribs, probably caused by a blow or a fall from a height, as well as fractures in her feet.

The sisters shared rare abnormalities in their spines as well. Researchers say this pattern indicates that their parents and the broader royal family were closely related.

"These injuries were most likely caused by accidents, falls, hard blows, or other impacts linked to an active lifestyle, whether through hunting, military training, or other demanding activities," said Hashesh. "What is remarkable is that the injuries healed well, which suggests they had access to advanced medical care for their time."

The fact that these injuries healed successfully provides another clue about royal life. Despite experiencing significant physical trauma, the princesses appear to have received medical treatment that allowed them to recover.

Reconstructing the Lives of Egypt's Royal Women

There are still important limits to what researchers can learn from the remains. The loss of the princesses' skulls restricts the kinds of analyses that can be performed, and the team has not yet completed every type of investigation it hopes to conduct.

One planned approach is stable isotope analysis, which could provide additional information about diet and help researchers better understand evidence of nutritional deficiencies.

"Our dream would be to go far beyond simply identifying the Dahshur royals," said Hashesh. "We would try to tell their full life stories, their families, health, and even their political roles, with as much detail as possible. Beyond the science, we would preserve the remains, create 3D prints for teaching and virtual exhibitions, and display them alongside their jewelry, weapons, and funerary objects. All of this would be done with respect, ensuring the remains are presented ethically, just as they were originally buried.

"Their objects and jewelry are truly fascinating, breathtaking in their craftsmanship. Yet, while archaeologists have long focused on preserving these treasures, the people themselves were often forgotten. Our study seeks to change that."
articles.reasoning: The article reveals new scientific insights into the active, physically demanding lives of ancient Egyptian royal women, challenging previous assumptions and highlighting their roles in archery and possibly military training. This discovery broadens understanding of historical gender roles and royal life, providing meaningful cultural and educational value. The research also emphasizes respectful preservation and ethical presentation of ancient remains, which benefits society's appreciation of history.
articles.personality_title: Ancient Egyptian princesses were skilled archers and warriors, new study finds
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – For a long time, scientists thought the weapons buried with ancient Egyptian princesses were just decorations for their tombs. These princesses lived during Egypt's Middle Kingdom, around 4,000 years ago, and their tombs contained bows, arrows, daggers, and maces.

**What happened** – Researchers studied six royal mummies found in Dahshur, Egypt, including four sisters who were daughters of Pharaoh Amenemhat II. By examining their bones, scientists discovered signs that these women used weapons regularly. Their bones showed strong muscle attachments and healed injuries from active, physical activities like archery and possibly hunting or military training.

**Impact** – This research changes how we understand the roles of ancient Egyptian royal women. Instead of only being ceremonial figures, these princesses were physically trained warriors. Their bones tell a story of strength and skill, showing they practiced demanding activities that shaped their bodies. It also shows they received good medical care to heal their injuries, revealing more about their daily lives.

**What's next step** – Scientists plan to use new techniques like stable isotope analysis to learn about the princesses’ diets and health. They also want to create 3D models of the mummies and display them respectfully with their jewelry and weapons to help people learn more about these royal women’s stories.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Ancient Egyptian princesses were not just royal figures but skilled archers and warriors, as shown by the marks on their bones and the weapons buried with them.
articles.personality_title_fr: Des princesses égyptiennes anciennes étaient archères et guerrières, révèle une nouvelle étude
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – Pendant longtemps, les scientifiques ont pensé que les armes enterrées avec les princesses égyptiennes anciennes n’étaient que des décorations pour leurs tombes. Ces princesses vivaient pendant le Moyen Empire d’Égypte, il y a environ 4 000 ans, et leurs tombes contenaient des arcs, des flèches, des poignards et des masses.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Des chercheurs ont étudié six momies royales découvertes à Dahchour, en Égypte, dont quatre sœurs filles du pharaon Amenemhat II. En examinant leurs os, ils ont trouvé des signes qu’elles utilisaient régulièrement des armes. Leurs os montraient des muscles forts et des blessures guéries liées à des activités physiques intenses comme le tir à l’arc et peut-être la chasse ou l’entraînement militaire.

**Impact** – Cette recherche change notre compréhension des rôles des femmes royales égyptiennes. Ce ne sont pas seulement des figures cérémoniales, mais des guerrières entraînées. Leurs os racontent une histoire de force et de compétence, montrant qu’elles faisaient des activités exigeantes qui ont façonné leur corps. Cela montre aussi qu’elles ont reçu de bons soins médicaux pour guérir leurs blessures, donnant plus d’informations sur leur vie quotidienne.

**Prochaine étape** – Les scientifiques prévoient d’utiliser de nouvelles techniques comme l’analyse isotopique pour en apprendre plus sur leur alimentation et leur santé. Ils veulent aussi créer des modèles 3D des momies et les exposer avec leurs bijoux et armes pour mieux raconter leur histoire.

**Phrase clé** – Les princesses égyptiennes anciennes n’étaient pas seulement des figures royales, mais des archères et guerrières compétentes, comme le montrent leurs os et les armes enterrées avec elles.
articles.personality_title_es: Antiguas princesas egipcias eran arqueras y guerreras, revela nuevo estudio
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Durante mucho tiempo, los científicos pensaron que las armas enterradas con las princesas egipcias antiguas eran solo decoraciones para sus tumbas. Estas princesas vivieron durante el Reino Medio de Egipto, hace unos 4,000 años, y sus tumbas contenían arcos, flechas, dagas y mazas.

**Qué pasó** – Investigadores estudiaron seis momias reales encontradas en Dahshur, Egipto, incluyendo cuatro hermanas hijas del faraón Amenemhat II. Al examinar sus huesos, encontraron señales de que estas mujeres usaban armas regularmente. Sus huesos mostraban músculos fuertes y heridas curadas por actividades físicas intensas como el tiro con arco y posiblemente la caza o entrenamiento militar.

**Impacto** – Esta investigación cambia cómo entendemos los roles de las mujeres reales egipcias. No solo eran figuras ceremoniales, sino guerreras entrenadas. Sus huesos cuentan una historia de fuerza y habilidad, mostrando que practicaban actividades exigentes que moldearon sus cuerpos. También muestra que recibían buen cuidado médico para sanar sus heridas, revelando más sobre su vida diaria.

**Próximos pasos** – Los científicos planean usar nuevas técnicas como el análisis de isótopos estables para aprender sobre la dieta y salud de las princesas. También quieren crear modelos 3D de las momias y exhibirlas respetuosamente con sus joyas y armas para ayudar a contar sus historias.

**Frase clave** – Las antiguas princesas egipcias no solo fueron figuras reales, sino arqueras y guerreras hábiles, como muestran sus huesos y las armas enterradas con ellas.
articles.image_prompt: A warm, detailed painting of six intricately crafted ancient Egyptian weapons—bows with taut strings, arrows with feathered fletching, ornate daggers, and maces—arranged respectfully on a smooth stone surface beside delicate gold and gemstone royal jewelry, all softly illuminated by gentle, natural light that highlights their craftsmanship and suggests the strength and active lives of the princesses who once wielded them.

articles.title: The millennials swapping doom-scrolling for gardening
articles.summary: Young people say gardening offers joy, serenity and a sense of community.
articles.content:
"I was born in '95, so my generation are the kind of ones who know what it's like to grow up with both analogue life and digital culture," said Hannah, from Newport.

She said hobbies such as cooking, sewing and gardening were her generation's "rejection of this hyper-digital world that feels really all-consuming".

She said it was a "tough time for young people" due to the cost of living, climate change, a "dire" jobs market and AI.

"I'm not saying we've had it harder than all other generations," she said.

"But it is challenging being young and maybe having different expectations to those that our parents and grandparents' generations had, and different opportunities."

Hannah said gardening offered a "safe space" to "take control of your little space of land or your balcony or your pots in the kitchen or whatever you're able to have".

It became that for her, she said, when she experienced the loss of her father and grandmother in 2023.

"I didn't use gardening as a conscious means of therapy but I kind of just found myself out here, pottering around," she said.

"It's cliché but kind of creating and nourishing new life and new growth is just really the circle of life."
articles.reasoning: The article highlights a meaningful positive social trend where young people are turning to gardening as a way to find joy, mental well-being, and community connection amid challenging societal conditions. This shift away from digital overload toward nurturing life and nature has broad emotional and social benefits, especially for mental health and community cohesion, though it is not a formal policy or large-scale breakthrough.
articles.personality_title: Young people find peace and purpose in gardening amid tough times
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – Many young people today face challenges like expensive living costs, climate worries, tough job markets, and the rise of artificial intelligence. These pressures make everyday life difficult and stressful.

**What happened** – Instead of spending all their time online, some young adults, including Hannah from Newport, are turning to gardening. Gardening gives them a way to relax, feel in control, and connect with nature. For Hannah, it became especially important after losing close family members in 2023.

**Impact** – This trend shows how gardening helps young people find calm and happiness in a busy, digital world. It offers a simple way to care for something living and build a sense of community. Gardening also supports mental health by providing a peaceful activity that helps people cope with stress and loss.

**What’s next step** – As more young people discover gardening, communities might see stronger connections and more green spaces. This could lead to more support for gardening programs and shared gardens, helping others find the same benefits.

**One-sentence takeaway** – Many young people are choosing gardening to find peace, control, and community in a challenging world.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les jeunes trouvent paix et sens dans le jardinage malgré les temps difficiles
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – De nombreux jeunes font face aujourd’hui à des défis comme le coût de la vie élevé, les inquiétudes climatiques, un marché du travail difficile et la montée de l’intelligence artificielle. Ces pressions rendent la vie quotidienne stressante.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Plutôt que de passer tout leur temps en ligne, certains jeunes adultes, comme Hannah de Newport, se tournent vers le jardinage. Le jardinage leur permet de se détendre, de se sentir maîtres de leur espace et de se connecter à la nature. Pour Hannah, cela a été particulièrement important après la perte de proches en 2023.

**Impact** – Cette tendance montre que le jardinage aide les jeunes à trouver calme et bonheur dans un monde numérique chargé. C’est une manière simple de prendre soin d’un être vivant et de créer du lien social. Le jardinage soutient aussi la santé mentale en offrant une activité apaisante pour gérer stress et deuil.

**Prochaine étape** – À mesure que davantage de jeunes découvrent le jardinage, les communautés pourraient renforcer leurs liens et développer des espaces verts. Cela pourrait encourager le soutien à des programmes de jardinage et à des jardins partagés, pour aider d’autres à profiter des mêmes bienfaits.

**Phrase clé** – De nombreux jeunes choisissent le jardinage pour trouver paix, contrôle et communauté dans un monde difficile.
articles.personality_title_es: Los jóvenes encuentran paz y propósito en la jardinería en tiempos difíciles
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – Muchos jóvenes hoy enfrentan desafíos como el alto costo de vida, preocupaciones climáticas, un mercado laboral complicado y el avance de la inteligencia artificial. Estas presiones hacen que la vida diaria sea estresante.

**Qué pasó** – En lugar de pasar todo su tiempo en línea, algunos adultos jóvenes, como Hannah de Newport, están optando por la jardinería. La jardinería les brinda una forma de relajarse, sentirse en control y conectarse con la naturaleza. Para Hannah, fue especialmente importante después de perder a familiares cercanos en 2023.

**Impacto** – Esta tendencia muestra cómo la jardinería ayuda a los jóvenes a encontrar calma y felicidad en un mundo digital saturado. Ofrece una manera sencilla de cuidar algo vivo y crear sentido de comunidad. La jardinería también apoya la salud mental al proporcionar una actividad tranquila para manejar el estrés y el duelo.

**Próximo paso** – A medida que más jóvenes descubran la jardinería, las comunidades podrían fortalecer sus lazos y aumentar los espacios verdes. Esto podría llevar a más apoyo para programas de jardinería y jardines compartidos, ayudando a otros a obtener los mismos beneficios.

**Frase clave** – Muchos jóvenes eligen la jardinería para encontrar paz, control y comunidad en un mundo desafiante.
articles.image_prompt: A cozy balcony garden at golden hour, filled with vibrant potted plants, a small wooden table with gardening tools gently scattered, and a pair of worn gardening gloves resting beside a sprouting seedling—soft, warm light envelops the scene, evoking nurturing growth and quiet healing in a simple, natural palette.
